newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Generali sets offer for Leumi Insurance.
newsitem.headline: Generali sets offer for Leumi Insurance.

text.p: Assicurazioni Generali SpA said on Thursday it had set its $308 million tender offering for shares in Israel's Leumi Insurance Holdings for next week.

In a filing with the Israeli Securities Authority, Generali said it would offer shareholders 3.2755 shekels ($0.97) each for 317,124,199 shares in Leumi Insurance, or up to 42.2 percent of any one shareholders' total holding.
The offer presents a 29 percent premium of Leumi Insurance's current share price, which closed at 2.54 shekels on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange on Wednesday.
Generali said the final offer price, whose total value is 1.04 billion shekels, would be adjusted for inflation after publication of the February consumer price index on Friday.
The Securities Authority may also require changes in the terms, a spokesman said.

The offer applies to those holding Leumi Insurance shares at the end of the business day on March 18, the notice said. A spokesman said shareholders could apply for the tender in the following two days, with payment scheduled for April 30.
If fully subscribed, the tender would leave Generali with about 57 percent of Leumi Insurance Holdings, Israel's biggest insurance group.
The acquisition has been shadowed by accusations by Israeli lawmakers and others that Generali has failed to honour life insurance policies taken out by people who subsequently died in the Holocaust.

Members of the insurance sub-committee of Israel's parliamentary finance committee have threatened to call for a boycott of Leumi Insurance's main subsidiary Migdal. A Generali spokesman termed the protests "not relevant" to the tender offer.
Last week a Generali spokesman in Milan said the company could not be held responsible for claims of Eastern European Holocaust victims, saying they should be made to the governments of the region.
The tender offer is part of a multifaceted deal under which Israel's Bank Leumi is reducing its holdings in Leumi Insurance and Africa Israel Investments to under 25 percent to meet bank reform laws.
Leumi will be selling part of its Leumi Insurance Holding in the offer.
